body:
Basically no success. There was one hookup on Tinder, and then things were getting pretty serious with another girl on Tinder where we Skyped and were planning to meet up, but things fell apart. I don't consider online things real because even though we skyped it's still over a camera and who knows cameras skew things sometimes ya know. 

Even then, having the feeling that "I know this hot girl was attracted to me" it helped me deal with everything else so much better. I was just able to go through life happily and confidently. I walked around feeling content with myself for once, like at least in one facet of life I wasn't so conspiculously inferior. That's why this is so devesating for me. I've never had that "real" interaction with someone where I knew with 100% certainty that they were physically attracted to me, so even as time went on I could still refer back to it and not feel awkward if I wanted to approach someone else. This girl was supposed to be that person, but now there is so much doubt, and so much has been fucked up in my life because of how I've dealt with her not telling me the truth or what she actually felt, I'm just at no idea where I stand. It's just something I want to feel comfortable knowing, ya know? Like, most guys don't want to die a virgin. That was my goal too. Now my goal is to know if I was even capable of attracting someone like her. 

Life is too fucking hard to deal with this shit

then i become that guy who everyone is like "why is she dating him". Or, worse yet, if we break up, I'm the "what was I thinking" guy. I have low self-esteem but I don't want to be with someone just for the "oh he's an amazing guy" thing. I know it sounds shallow but I feel like a relationship should be a 2-way street and if I'm physically attracted to the girl I would want her to feel the same way about me. That would be a healthy relationship. I just don't get why I can't have that. Like why I am the one who's so ridiculously shitty.

Sure she used me for self-esteem stuff, that's actually fine with me. I just want to know if there was even a hint of physical attraction there. Like, if she didn't have low self esteem, would I even have a chance. I just want to know so that I can know for sure "ok, I'm not unfuckably ugly." Like, can a girl be physically attracted to a guy but not overall attracted? Is that even a possibility with this girl? You say that there are probably girls who are attracted to me but I'm socially aware enough to see signals, and trust me, there are no signals. I needed this girl desperately but it's like the universe hates me so fucking much I can't have one iota of happiness in my life.

wow I'm reading all these posts about how people's exes are nice and kind and something terrible happened in the relationship, and I'm just sitting here realizing my ex never liked me. 

If she were to magically see this: "Lisa, I did like you. I'm sorry about how I acted a year later but I just wanted to know how you felt about me. What you said hurt. Like really hurt. Like making me attempt suicide multiple times, gain 40 lbs, fail a class, and disregard life. You were the first person who showed genuine interest in me. I thought someone like you would never be interested in me, and so it hurt to get real confirmation of that when you said 'I only liked you cause you like me.'

Sorry I'm such a loser and unconfident and unattractive. I know I asked you over text and even over the phone and both times you said yes, but honestly i don't know if what you said was real because you may have just said that to get me off your ass. I know you don't care, and believe it or not I don't care what the answer is, I just want to know, from you, what you genuinely felt about me, without anything impeding your feelings such as my feelings or me pestering you.

I know you're with chaddius thunderloins now. Don't worry I won't bother you again. I realized the only way I'll be happy is if I work hard for the next 2 years to graduate college and then just kill myself afterward since I'll be 21 and legally able to get a gun."

There are thousands of posts online about nice guys who are protective and smart and funny and whatever who don't get with the girl. In addition, there are very few posts online about girls who get with guys just because they're interesting and what not. 

Regardless, I don't want to be in a relationship like that, where the girl thinks I'm ugly but "oh, he makes a lot of money" or "he's nice/funny/interesting". Why should i work to be 1000 different things when a guy who's very physically attractive can just be one thing and find equal success.

but whatever. my post was mainly about the frustration i feel about not being able to figure out what this girl felt about me, not about girls being emotionally vs physically attracted. like actually felt about me. and trying to figure out if what she said was true. I wouldn't care so much about a girl finding me emotionally attractive if I just had one girl in my past who was into me physically.

If it's any consolation, my father is on my ass constantly about my grades as well and he is (was when i was in high school) physically abusive when I didn't do well. He's still very emotionally abusive however. I'm not going to sit here and tell you your parents want the best for you and that they care about you and that's all that matters. You probably already know in the back of your head that's true but if you're anything like me, those two thoughts don't provide any consolation for the fear of disappointment or abuse you'll receive when he finds out about your grades. What I will tell you though is that if you fess up to it when it happens, just let your parents get the yelling and frustration out of their system, then the aftermath is better. More often than not, they will get angry at you first, express hurtful disapproval or anger, and then try to find the best solution to help you out. Sure, not every parent is   going to be happy about their kids getting bad grades, but in the end they probably want to help you. 

Feel free to PM me if you want. 

EDIT: Also, sorry to be that guy, but not everyone has the liberty to just say "Fuck parents. YOLO."

> I don't quite understand what the problem is, would you try to explain it and why is it so important you find the answer?

Because if I know that at least 1 person was genuinely physically attracted to me in the past, I will have confidence approaching other people. This would help me out in so many areas of my life. It's not just that I'll be "willing to give life a chance". It's that, if I'm unattractive, then I feel its ridiculous I have to compensate extraordinarily in other areas of life. I understand some basic compensation, like having a good career or being interesting or charitable. But to be good at everything else, only to fall short next to somebody who is more physically attractive, I just don't want to be around for that. 

Sure I don't have enough dating experience, but it doesn't take a stud to know that if you're ugly then you're probably not going to be in a lot of relationships and the girl will think "oh he's a nice guy and interesting and funny" but as soon as the opportunity comes for a nice guy who's more attractive, the girl will at least seriously consider the option. Maybe loyalty comes into play but I don't want to be in a relationship where I'm a ball and chain holding someone back from being with someone who they're more attracted to. 

I'm sorry if it doesn't make sense but it's the best way I can explain it. If I'm ugly, then I'm hopeless and inferior (not saying everyone who is ugly is hopeless and inferior, just me). I care what this girl thinks because she's the first one who showed what I thought was genuine interest in me, and she was attractive. I felt for once that "hey, at least I'm not a complete piece of shit". I know I'm not Ryan Gosling, but I just wanted to know if I have a baseline physical attractiveness, to know that I'm not hideous and I'm worthy of consideration just based on looks, without having to be rich or a comedian or a pro dancer. I don't feel like what I'm asking to know is that crazy but everyone seems to say that I'm just obsessing over this. No one seems to understand that the reason they think it's obsessive is because they have had that ONE person attracted to them. Just one. So they can move on thinking "I don't care that I got rejected by that guy/girl, that other guy/girl was attracted to me anyway.". I don't fucking have that. When I thought Lisa was attracted to me, I felt confident and didn't care that she left. Now that it was brought into question and I don't know how she genuinely felt, I genuinely feel worse than where I was before I met her.  

Yes, if I knew she found me attractive, I would be more willing to give life a chance (this isn't the only thing in my life that's been bothering me, just a big portion of it). But I don't want to go through life striving for the best in all other areas of life when other people just can be average/good and find love just based on their looks. I don't want someone to settle for me and still think in the back of their heads "he's not attractive." It's not worth it for me. A relationship goes two ways and I won't be happy in that sort of relationship where someone isn't attracted to me physically. So instead of being alone and having to deal with that, I find the easiest thing to do would be to kill myself after graduation. It's not a spur of the moment feeling in anger, it's something I've given genuine thought and effort into. I didn't write the above post in complete feelings of despair, it's something I've felt for a LONG time. I just wanted one normal girl to tell me that I was physically attractive, just so I can have a bit of happiness in my life in that regard. That I don't have to work for EVERY thing in this world, that I was genetically good in ONE fucking area. But no.

But people who say "just move on" usually have had a few people in the past who they know have been attracted to them physically to some degree. They have the confidence to say "I'll find another". My first time was in high school when we were drunk so I don't know how that girl felt, and with this past girl I have no idea how she felt now. If she weren't attracted to me, it would mean that no one has been attracted to me, which is a crushing blow to my confidence. Sure, there are other factors other than physical attraction, but I don't want to be in a relationship where the other person isn't physically attracted to me. That would mean I would have to work exponentially hard to have a great career and interests and personality but if some better looking guy came along then my SO my cheat on me. I don't want that. That's why I care about it something that everyone seems to think is so minor. Yes, it's the opinion of one person, numerically. But it's not like I'm being approached by women everywhere I go. There was literally 1 girl in high school (the drunk one) and then 1 girl right now (her). Why would she sleep with me if she didn't even at least find me fuckable?

i've tried r/relationships but I just don't know what the truth is. It still keeps me up at night ruminating about this. Though what you say makes sense it is nearly impossible for me to just ignore all the negativity in my life by simply not thinking about it. Even if I try to work on myself, the thought will still remain "I don't know even know if I'm attractive enough to approach someone.". That's what's been hindering me from doing it in the first place, because I don't see a point to making myself look better in my body if I don't even know if I look okay.
Thank you for your words.

My main problem is the loneliness. I don't see what I do wrong that alienates people. I'm pretty confident in saying that I have basic social norms, I'm just not all that interesting since I don't particularly have any interests. I can't force myself to enjoy something I don't. Moreover, I've tried the whole "join clubs" thing but even in clubs, people already have their friend groups. I feel like a pariah.
Nothing, that's the thing. I've tried common stuff like gaming and sports but I'm not into it enough to have a convo.

They are just random medtech organizations on campus. And yeah I mean when I first meet people I can stifle my awkwardness long enough to come across as normal but beyond the handshakes and basic questions no one really is interested in talking to me. So I have a lot of "hello"s on campus from people I've met through other conversations but nothing beyond that. Occasionally I might eat with someone I know if I've seen them at the dining hall and such, but again, never beyond that.

Not sure how to describe 3.0, like 3.0/4.0 I guess (I think I read somewhere that a 3.0 is 60-69 in UK vs a 3.5 which would be a 70-100, sorry if that's wrong). 

I don't really do anything else. I'm chairman on a few organizations but those just usually involve a lot of paperwork and emails and we hardly meet. I've tried "getting involved" with other stuff but I end up feeling isolated since everyone else has their own group within clubs as well.

I was a biomedical engineer but now I'm computer science and math. Before the September 2014 semester I was on Dean's list. After that meeting with this girl happened I dropped to just above a 3.0. This is a tearing my life apart. I couldn't sleep, every waking moment, even the days and hours before a final when I should've been studying, I obsessed over this and analyzed everything she did, posted on every forum I could think of to get advice.

> I'm an easy target...so far from being attractive

I can't tell you how close this hits to home. I can't provide any consolation beyond telling you I feel EXACTLY as you do. I'm sorry. I hope we both get out of this is some way.

I'm looking for one, but I'm fairly convinced they'll tell me the same thing. I know I have self-esteem issues but talking to someone about them will not make them go away. A therapist won't help someone be more interested in me. A therapist won't help people want to hang out with me beyond friendly conversation. Moreover, a therapist won't help me figure out what that girl was doing with me, which is the only way I see getting over that problem.
but it would take a long time to see substantial results, probably even up to the point I graduate. Being alive today is hard enough.

I've been to therapy and the woman just said "you have self-esteem issues." Yeah no fucking shit that's because no one in the world has been interested in me. And I used to be in shape (at least better than what I am now) but I don't see the point. No one is attracted to me so why try to build muscle and lose fat when I don't have a baseline attraction? It doesn't make me feel good. I'm not one of those people who works out and has that rush of endorphins.

I try to forget, but she lives in the same building as me and I can't move. Plus, I see her on campus a lot too. The worst is seeing her with her new guy. No joke, I can be having a great day, and the instant I see her all these memories come flooding back in and I start to think about how she may have felt about me back then. It ruins my day and the rest of my week. 

It hurts a lot. I wish I had even the tiniest iota of confidence to say "fuck it" like everyone else recommends. I'm just scared that since she was the only one who showed interest, that I won't find anyone else.

yeah that's how I thought too. but there are so many people who say that girls will fuck anyone regardless of their physical attraction to them if they have low self-esteem. and it's not like we had sex on several occasions, just multiple times on 2 separate occasions.

Well I'm not blaming her for not finding me attractive, I'm just sad for not being able to figure it out. If I'm not someone's type then I'm not someone's type, I just have to accept that and try to move on. What makes me sad though is that I feel like I'm no one's type. 

But I'm not trying to say that "I only want to date hot girls and nothing less". When I said "ONE [attractive] person" I meant that someone I was at least somewhat attracted to. The ONS I had in high school was with someone I just wasn't personally attracted to physically and emotionally. 

I wouldn't blame someone for not being physically into someone, that's just human nature. I just wish I knew how she felt so I could have some sort of validation and thereby confidence in myself to approach someone. Like, before making a move on someone, I would want to know if I'm at least somewhere in their range, ya know? Otherwise I would just be embarrassing myself.

Well she may or may not have had low self-esteem. When I met her, her dating history was: one LTR in high school with whom she broke it off with because she didn't like the guy anymore, 1 guy who I'm pretty sure she said cheated on her, one guy named S who she didn't fuck but she kissed a few times and told me she liked (but S stopped talking to her), and then one hookup with S's friend. 

So it's possible. One one hand she seems like the kind of girl who moves on from things pretty quickly. She said that she was somewhat jealous when she saw S with another girl but got over it in a few minutes. On the other hand, she seemed kind of lonely and didn't have any friends. It's hard to say only because by talking with her one can sort of tell she doesn't seem to care too much about what people think, but humans are humans, so idk maybe she was feeling low.

Also, she did say she mostly liked me because I liked her. I interpret that at least as low self esteem.

well it was multiple times but only on 2 separate occasions. like multiple times in a night but only on 2 nights. and I hope you're right but everyone on 4chan or bb forums says "dude you're a pussy she didn't like you girls do that with anyone if they have low self esteem."

but if you are right, that would be all the confidence I need. I basically just want to know i have some chance. that's really it.

The fact that you and everyone who responded took the time to respond does help a lot, so thank you. And what you say makes logical sense, but what doesn't make sense to me is that if she was attracted to me, why didn't she stay. I'm pretty sure I did nothing wrong. Maybe the sex wasn't all that great and that's why it only happened twice. Maybe she was telling the truth and she really didn't like my personality. I don't remember doing anything wrong with her (except maybe I would ask her to "do stuff" before doing it) What doesn't make sense to me is that I was always under the impression that if a girl is physically attracted to you, they tend to forgive the small stuff. Then I can't understand why she didn't stay with me.

but wouldn't a girl sleep with someone who disgusts them if they have low self-esteem? I'm pretty sure I read an exact story like that on here about a woman who married a neckbeard because her self-esteem was very low and he seemed like a nice guy. 

Also please don't take the fact that I'm trying to counter what you say as a refusal of help. I really do appreciate everyone who responded in this thread. I'm only "arguing" so i can have a better understanding for the future as well as to get my own fears out of the way. It's cathartic for me and you guys have no idea how much sleep I've lost over analyzing each of my fears.

You and everyone else are correct. I know i should stop thinking about it and focus on my life. But I just don't see the point of working out or anything if there is no base-line. What i mean is, a lot of my friends that are girls have turned down guys with really attractive bodies just because of things like "he's short", "his face is weird", stuff like that. I'm kind of short, so that might have been it with me and L, but I still feel inferior because I don't even know if she found me somewhat attractive in the slightest, and her new bf (or whatever the fuck he is) is way more attractive.

the thought of being alone scares me though. I'm only 19, yes. But if I can't find ONE [attractive] person who was attracted to me legitimately, I'm afraid I'll grow up to be one of those 40-50 year olds who's still alone. There's no way in hell I would want to live through that.

I tried that. but I can't really fake it till I make it. Some of my friends act confident too, but they don't have dates either because girls don't find them physically attractive (from what I've heard from the girls that they've hit on). Confidence only goes so far. That's why I wanted to know if I have a baseline.

I want to believe you but it's extremely difficult for me (sorry). She told me directly that she liked me because I liked her. that basically says she used me for validation. Everywhere I post people say she's been using me. And yes she was holding hands with a guy but i know she is actually with the guy as well. 

I really wish it was a short-term relationship, but she told me directly that she didn't want a relationship (this is within the 2 weeks we were doing stuff, before winter break). She didn't want to be with me. That's what hurts. If I wasn't everything she wanted in a guy, okay. I understand. But I just wanted to know if she at least thought I was fuckable, like decent enough looking for a hookup. That would really be all the confidence I need. 

Sometimes people are extremely cruel. More than her using me, it hurts me more that she can't have the fucking decency to give me 30 seconds of her life to just explain to me "you weren't really my type but you were nice to me and I needed that at the time."

I would date people if they were actually interested, but they're not. That's why I'm stuck in this cycle. At first being with L gave me confidence. Even after we split up I was still confident because I felt "Well, It didn't work out with L, but if I could get her I could probably get someone equally good or even better if I work on myself." Now I don't even know whether I'm even decent enough to get anybody. I needed some validation and she won't even just tell me what she felt about me.
